docs.title: España – Educación para la Salud: Marco Legal y Contexto Regulatorio (LOMLOE 2020)
1. Panorama del Sistema Educativo Español / Overview of the Spanish Education System
1.1 Datos Básicos
docs.text: Parámetro Valor País España / Spain (ES) Población ~47,4 millones (2024) Idioma oficial Español (castellano); co-oficiales: catalán, valenciano, gallego, vasco, etc. Tipo de sistema educativo Descentralizado – MEFP establece enseñanzas mínimas (55–65%); Comunidades Autónomas (CCAA) completan el currículo Número de CCAA 17 Comunidades Autónomas (con competencias educativas propias) Escolarización obligatoria 6–16 años Etapas del sistema educativo post-primaria ESO (12–16; 4 cursos) → Bachillerato (16–18; 2 cursos) o Formación Profesional Examen de acceso universitario EBAU (Evaluación de Bachillerato para el Acceso a la Universidad) Autoridad curricular nacional MEFP (Ministerio de Educación, Formación Profesional y Deportes)

docs.title: 1.2 Peculiaridad del Sistema: La Descentralización
docs.text:
España tiene un sistema educativo fuertemente descentralizado. Las Comunidades Autónomas (como Cataluña, Andalucía, Madrid, País Vasco, etc.) tienen competencias para: - Completar entre el 35–45% adicional del currículo (sobre las enseñanzas mínimas del MEFP) - Establecer sus propias materias optativas de carácter autonómico - Definir el calendario escolar y la organización del sistema en su territorio - Desarrollar programas propios de salud escolar

Implicación para la investigación: La educación para la salud en España tiene una capa nacional (LOMLOE + Reales Decretos) y una capa autonómica. Este documento cubre principalmente la capa nacional.

docs.title: 2.1 Datos de la Ley
docs.text: Dato Valor Nombre completo Ley Orgánica 3/2020, de 29 de diciembre, por la que se modifica la Ley Orgánica 2/2006, de 3 de mayo, de Educación (LOE) Denominación común LOMLOE ("Ley Celaá") Fecha de publicación 30 de diciembre de 2020 BOE referencia BOE-A-2020-17264 Entrada en vigor general 19 de enero de 2021 URL oficial https://www.boe.es/eli/es/lo/2020/12/29/3

docs.title: 2.2 Pricipios Pedagógicos Relevantes para la Salud (Art. 2 y Preámbulo LOMLOE)
docs.text: La LOMLOE establece los siguientes principios del sistema educativo directamente relacionados con la salud: - La educación integral del alumnado – física, afectiva, emocional, intelectual y social - La igualdad efectiva entre hombres y mujeres y la no discriminación - La educación para la salud, incluida la afectivo-sexual, como elemento transversal de todas las etapas - La educación ambiental y la conciencia del cambio climático - La educación para la ciudadanía democrática - La prevención de la violencia de género y el respeto a los derechos humanos

docs.title: 2.3 Educación para la Salud en la LOMLOE – Carácter Transversal
docs.text:
La LOMLOE no establece la "Educación para la Salud" como una asignatura independiente y obligatoria. En su lugar:

"Las Administraciones educativas adoptarán medidas para que la actividad física y la dieta equilibrada formen parte del comportamiento infantil y juvenil. A estos efectos, dichas Administraciones promoverán la práctica diaria de deporte y ejercicio físico por parte de los alumnos y alumnas durante la jornada escolar, en los términos y condiciones que, siguiendo las recomendaciones de los organismos competentes, garanticen un desarrollo adecuado para favorecer una vida activa, saludable y autónoma..."

Los elementos de salud se integran de forma transversal en todas las materias, especialmente en: - Biología y Geología (ESO) - Educación Física (ESO y Bachillerato) - Educación en Valores Cívicos y Éticos (ESO) - Biología, Anatomía y Fisiología / Biología (Bachillerato)

docs.title: 3.1 Real Decreto 217/2022 – ESO
docs.text:
Dato Valor Nombre completo Real Decreto 217/2022, de 29 de marzo, por el que se establece la ordenación y las enseñanzas mínimas de la Educación Secundaria Obligatoria Publicación BOE BOE núm. 76, de 30 de marzo de 2022 BOE referencia BOE-A-2022-4975 URL BOE https://www.boe.es/eli/es/rd/2022/03/29/217 Implantación Cursos 1º y 3º ESO: septiembre 2022; Cursos 2º y 4º ESO: septiembre 2023

Elementos clave relacionados con la salud en el RD 217/2022: - Define el "Perfil de salida" del alumnado – competencias esperadas al final de la enseñanza básica, incluyendo: "emprender acciones fundamentadas científicamente para promover la salud física, mental y social, y preservar el medio ambiente" - Introduce el modelo de competencias clave (8 competencias: CL, CP, STEM, CPSAA, CC, CE, CCEC, CD) - Establece los "saberes básicos" (contenidos) de cada materia, incluyendo los relacionados con la salud - Obliga a los centros a trabajar la educación afectivo-sexual de forma transversal

docs.title: 3.2 Real Decreto 243/2022 – Bachillerato
docs.text:
Dato Valor Nombre completo Real Decreto 243/2022, de 5 de abril, por el que se establecen la ordenación y las enseñanzas mínimas del Bachillerato Publicación BOE BOE núm. 82, de 6 de abril de 2022 BOE referencia BOE-A-2022-5521 URL BOE https://www.boe.es/eli/es/rd/2022/04/05/243 Implantación 1º Bachillerato: septiembre 2022; 2º Bachillerato: septiembre 2023

Objetivos explícitos de Bachillerato relacionados con la salud (Art. 3 del RD 243/2022):

"Consolidar una madurez personal, afectivo-sexual y social que les permita actuar de forma respetuosa, responsable y autónoma... prever, detectar y resolver pacíficamente los conflictos personales, familiares y sociales, así como las posibles situaciones de violencia."

docs.title: 4. Historia Legislativa de la Educación para la Salud en España
docs.text: Año Hito 1990 LOGSE – Primera mención explícita de la educación para la salud como eje transversal en el currículo 2006 LOE – Mantiene el carácter transversal; añade la ESO como etapa con perfil de competencias 2013 LOMCE ("Ley Wert") – Reduce contenidos de educación para la ciudadanía; debilita el enfoque de salud integral 2020 LOMLOE ("Ley Celaá") – Restaura y amplía el enfoque integral; añade explícitamente "educación afectivo-sexual" como transversal 2022 Real Decretos 217/2022 (ESO) y 243/2022 (Bachillerato) – Despliegan el currículo LOMLOE 2022–2023 Implantación progresiva en todos los niveles de ESO y Bachillerato 2023 Aprobación de Ley Orgánica 10/2022 (Ley de Libertad Sexual) – Afecta a contenidos de educación afectivo-sexual

docs.text: Institución Rol en educación para la salud MEFP (Ministerio de Educación, Formación Profesional y Deportes) Legislación, enseñanzas mínimas, coordinación nacional Comunidades Autónomas (17) Desarrollo del currículo (35–45%), programas propios de salud escolar Ministerio de Sanidad Estrategias de salud pública; datos estadísticos; Encuesta de Salud de España (ESdE) INTEF (Instituto Nacional de Tecnologías Educativas y Formación del Profesorado) Recursos digitales para docentes; formación online AESAN (Agencia Española de Seguridad Alimentaria y Nutrición) Recursos sobre nutrición y hábitos alimentarios saludables para escuelas Centro Nacional de Salud Pública (CNSP) Estrategias de prevención y promoción de salud OMS/WHO España Datos internacionales; recomendaciones para programas de salud escolar

docs.title: España – Metodología de la Educación para la Salud y Estadísticas de Salud Juvenil (2022–2025)
1. Enfoque Pedagógico de la Educación para la Salud en España
1.1 El Modelo de Aprendizaje Basado en Competencias (LOMLOE)
docs.text:
La LOMLOE introduce un cambio pedagógico fundamental: del currículo centrado en contenidos al currículo centrado en competencias. Esto tiene implicaciones directas para la educación para la salud:

Antes (LOE/LOMCE): Los alumnos aprenden "qué es" la salud → conocimiento declarativo Ahora (LOMLOE): Los alumnos deben ser capaces de "actuar" en salud → conocimiento funcional y aplicado

Las ocho competencias clave que vertebran el currículo LOMLOE y su relación con la salud:

Competencia Clave Abreviatura Relación con la salud Competencia en Comunicación Lingüística CL Comprender y comunicar información sobre salud Competencia Plurilingüe CP Acceder a fuentes sobre salud en otros idiomas Competencia STEM STEM Pensamiento científico para decisiones de salud Competencia Digital CD Alfabetización digital en salud; evaluación de fuentes Competencia Personal, Social y de Aprender a Aprender CPSAA Autoconocimiento; regulación emocional; bienestar Competencia Ciudadana CC Salud pública; derechos en salud; sostenibilidad Competencia Emprendedora CE Autonomía en la gestión de la propia salud Competencia en Conciencia y expresión cultural CCEC Arte y cultura como vía para la salud emocional

docs.title: 1.2 Las Situaciones de Aprendizaje
docs.text:
El instrumento metodológico central de la LOMLOE son las "situaciones de aprendizaje" – contextos auténticos y significativos donde los alumnos aplican sus competencias.

En el ámbito de la salud, las situaciones de aprendizaje pueden incluir: - "Diseña un menú semanal saludable para tu clase con un presupuesto ajustado" - "Analiza una campaña publicitaria de bebidas energéticas: ¿qué mensajes envía sobre la salud?" - "Organiza una charla de sensibilización sobre salud mental para alumnos de 1º ESO" - "Investiga los datos sobre obesidad infantil en tu comunidad y propón medidas preventivas"

Este enfoque favorece el aprendizaje experiencial, contextualizado y crítico de la salud.

docs.title: 2.1 Aprendizaje Basado en Proyectos (ABP)
docs.text: El ABP es especialmente recomendado para abordar temas de salud complejos y transversales: - Proyectos de investigación sobre enfermedades prevalentes - Campañas de promoción de la salud en el centro - Análisis de casos clínicos o epidemiológicos - Proyectos de actividad física y bienestar comunitario

docs.title: 2.2 Metodologías Activas para Contenidos Sensibles
docs.text:
Para temas sensibles (salud mental, sexualidad, adicciones), se recomiendan:

Método Descripción Debate estructurado Análisis de distintas perspectivas sobre dilemas éticos en salud Análisis de casos Situaciones ficticias o reales (anonimizadas) para desarrollar empatía y pensamiento crítico Role-play Práctica de habilidades de comunicación en salud (pedir ayuda, hablar con el médico) Aprendizaje entre iguales (peer education) Alumnos de cursos superiores forman a sus compañeros en temas de salud Grupos de trabajo cooperativo Exploración de aspectos complementarios de un mismo problema de salud Portafolios digitales Registro del proceso de aprendizaje en salud (especialmente en EF y Biología)

docs.title: 2.3 Integración Digital
docs.text: El INTEF (Instituto Nacional de Tecnologías Educativas y Formación del Profesorado) proporciona recursos digitales para la enseñanza de la salud. Las herramientas recomendadas incluyen: - Plataforma educativa INTEF – recursos sobre educación afectivo-sexual, alimentación, salud mental - EducaLAB – laboratorio de innovación educativa del MEFP - Recursos de la OMS/OPS – materiales adaptados para escuelas - AESAN – recursos sobre nutrición para escolares - FAO – El plato de la alimentación saludable – para clases de Biología y EF

docs.title: 3. Programas Nacionales y Autonómicos de Salud Escolar
3.1 Programas Nacionales
docs.text: Programa Organismo Ámbito NAOS (Estrategia para la Nutrición, Actividad Física y Prevención de la Obesidad) AESAN / Ministerio de Sanidad Nutrición y actividad física en escuelas Forma Joven Junta de Andalucía (luego extendido a otras CCAA) Salud integral en adolescentes; atiende salud mental, sexual, adicciones PNSD (Plan Nacional sobre Drogas) Ministerio de Sanidad Prevención de adicciones; materiales para centros educativos Salut i Escola (Salud y Escuela) Cataluña Atención sanitaria en el entorno escolar; enfermería en centros Programa de Diagnóstico y Tratamiento de la Obesidad Infantil Ministerio de Sanidad / CCAA Detección precoz y prevención de la obesidad en escolares

docs.title: 3.2 Estrategia de Salud Sexual y Reproductiva (ESSR)
docs.text: El Ministerio de Sanidad coordina la Estrategia de Salud Sexual y Reproductiva, que incluye: - Formación docente en educación afectivo-sexual - Materiales didácticos para el profesorado - Coordinación con centros de atención primaria y planificación familiar - Datos epidemiológicos sobre embarazo adolescente e ITS

docs.title: 4. Formación del Profesorado en Educación para la Salud
4.1 Sistema de Formación Docente
docs.text:
En España, la formación del profesorado para содержание de salud no sigue un modelo tan centralizado como en Polonia (kwalifikacyjne studia podyplomowe) o Irlanda (Oide). Se articula a través de:

Formación inicial: - Los futuros profesores de Biología, Educación Física, Psicología, etc. incluyen didáctica de la salud en sus correspondientes másteres de formación del profesorado (MAES) - No hay una especialidad MAES específica en "educación para la salud"

Formación continua: - CEP (Centros de Profesores) – Red nacional de ~100 centros de formación permanente; ofrecen cursos sobre educación para la salud, educación afectivo-sexual, prevención de adicciones - INTEF – Cursos online gratuitos reconocidos para el profesorado; incluyen módulos sobre salud digital, nutrición, salud emocional - Comunidades Autónomas – Cada CCAA oferta su propia formación permanente a través de sus centros de apoyo al profesorado - Universidades – Formación de posgrado (másteres propios, certificados de extensión universitaria) en educación para la salud, psicología educativa, etc.

docs.title: 4.2 Reto de la Educación Afectivo-Sexual
docs.text: La formación del profesorado para la educación afectivo-sexual es el área más débil: - No existe formación sistemática universal para todos los docentes - La mayoría de cursos son ofertados voluntariamente por los CEP o por ONGs (como Fundación Triángulo, FELGTBI+, Planned Parenthood) - El nivel de cobertura varía significativamente entre CCAA y centros

docs.title: 5. Estadísticas de Salud de Adolescentes en España (2022–2024)
5.1 Datos Principales
docs.text:
Encuesta de Salud de España (ESdE) 2023 y otras fuentes:

docs.title: 6. Desafíos y Controversias en la Educación para la Salud en España
6.1 El Debate sobre la Educación Afectivo-Sexual
docs.text: La educación afectivo-sexual es el tema más polémico en el contexto español: - Postura gobierno (LOMLOE): educación afectivo-sexual obligatoria, transversal, inclusiva de diversidad LGBTBI+ - Postura oposición (PP, Vox): Recurso ante el Tribunal Constitucional contra contenidos LGBTBI+; defensa de la libertad de los padres para gestionar la educación sexual de sus hijos - Resultado: La ley está vigente, pero la implementación varía significativamente por CCAA (ej.: Madrid vs. Andalucía vs. País Vasco)

docs.title: 6.2 El Pin Parental
docs.text: Algunas CCAA (especialmente Madrid y Murcia, bajo gobiernos del PP) han debatido o implementado temporalmente el "pin parental" – derecho de los padres a vetar la asistencia de sus hijos a actividades complementarias sobre salud, diversidad u orientación sexual organizadas por ONGs en los colegios. Los tribunales han limitado su alcance.

docs.title: 6.3 La Fragmentación por Comunidades Autónomas
docs.text: La descentralización, aunque positiva en principio, genera enormes desigualdades en la educación para la salud: - Cataluña, País Vasco, Navarra: programas más desarrollados, mayor presupuesto, formación de profesorado más sólida - Comunidades menos ricas o con menor priorización política: programas más débiles, mayor dependencia del voluntarismo docente

Este registro lista todos los documentos fuente identificados para España en el proyecto OneHealth EU. This registry lists all source documents identified for Spain in the OneHealth EU project.

docs.title: System Overview
docs.text: Spain has a decentralised education system: the national ministry (MEFP) defines enseñanzas mínimas (55–65% of curriculum), while the 17 Comunidades Autónomas develop the remainder. Health education is integrated transversally across Biology and Geology, Physical Education (EPS), and Civic and Ethical Values. Spain also champions the Escuelas Promotoras de Salud model, linking human health to environmental health through a One Health lens.

docs.title: Finland – Terveystieto: FAQ, Implementation Context and 6-Country Comparative Analysis (2025)
1.1 Structure and Curriculum
docs.text:
Q: Is there a dedicated "Health Education" subject in Finland? A: Yes – Terveystieto (Health Education) is a mandatory, standalone, independent subject in Finnish schools: - Grades 7–9 of peruskoulu (basic education, ages 13–16): obligatory for all pupils - Lukio (general upper secondary, ages 16–19): 3 mandatory modules (TE1, TE2, TE3) - This makes Finland one of the very few EU countries with dedicated, mandatory health education at both lower and upper secondary level.

Q: When did Finland introduce health education as a separate subject? A: Finland's parliament passed legislation in 2001 making Terveystieto a mandatory independent subject. Implementation began in all schools in August 2004. The motivation was concern about worsening adolescent health trends and recognition that integrating health content into other subjects was insufficient.

Q: What qualifications do health education teachers need in Finland? A: Finnish health education teachers are required to hold: - Master's degree (5 years) - ≥60 ECTS in health education subject studies (aineopinnot) - ≥60 ECTS in pedagogical studies (pedagogiset opinnot)

This is equivalent to the requirement for physics or chemistry teachers – Health Education is treated as a rigorous academic subject, not a life skills activity.

Q: Can health education be examined in the Finnish Matriculation Examination (Ylioppilastutkinto)? A: Yes. Health Education is an optional subject in the ylioppilastutkinto (Baccalaureate-level national examination). Students who choose it must demonstrate health literacy – not just recall facts, but analyse, evaluate and apply health knowledge. This is unique in Europe.

Q: Are personal health behaviors assessed in Finnish Terveystieto? A: Explicitly no. The national curriculum states:

"Assessment shall not target the student's personal values, attitudes, temperament, or health behaviors."

Only health literacy (terveysosaaminen) is assessed – the ability to understand and critically analyse health phenomena.

docs.title: 1.2 Specific Topics
docs.text:
Q: How is sexual health education delivered in Finland? A: Sexual health is integrated into Terveystieto across all levels: - Grades 7–9 (S2): anatomy, puberty, contraception, STIs, sexual diversity, consent, online safety - Lukio TE1: sexual health as a lifelong resource; advanced contraception; STI epidemiology; healthy relationships - There is NO separate law required (unlike Portugal's Lei 60/2009 or France's law on 3 sessions). It is included in regular Terveystieto curriculum. - School nurses in many schools provide free condoms to students.

Q: How does Finland address the mental health crisis among girls? A: The THL Kouluterveyskysely 2023 revealed that 31–34% of 8th–9th grade girls report moderate-to-severe anxiety – a dramatically higher rate than boys (7–8%). Finland's response includes: - School psychologist (koulupsykologi) and social worker (koulukuraattori) in every school - National Mental Health Strategy 2020–2030 (STM) - Low-threshold services: Sekasin-chat (anonymous online mental health chat for youth) - 24/7 crisis line: 116 123 (Mieli ry) - This is addressed directly in Terveystieto curriculum (mental health as central theme)

Q: What is Finland's approach to bullying prevention? A: Finland developed KiVa Koulu – an internationally recognized, evidence-based anti-bullying program used in ~90% of Finnish basic education schools. THL 2023 data show bullying increased slightly (8–9% weekly bullying in grades 8–9), highlighting remaining challenges despite the program.

Q: How does the Finnish healthcare system support school health education? A: Finland has an integrated school healthcare system (kouluterveydenhuolto): - Mandatory health examinations in grades 1, 5, 8 (peruskoulu) and 1st year of lukio - School nurse (terveydenhoitaja) available daily, free, confidential - School doctor for more complex issues - All of this is free and universal – no socioeconomic barriers to access

docs.title: 2. Context of the Finnish Model (Historical and Policy)
2.1 Why Finland Introduced Terveystieto as a Separate Subject
docs.text: The 2001 parliamentary decision was motivated by: - Research showing that health content integrated into biology and PE was insufficient for developing health literacy - Worsening adolescent health trends in the 1990s (substance use, mental health) - International context: WHO recommendations for comprehensive health education - Finnish educational philosophy: all important competencies deserve dedicated subject status

docs.title: 2.2 The Nordic Welfare State Context
docs.text: The Finnish model of health education CANNOT be separated from the broader Nordic welfare state: - Universal healthcare: all students have access to free school health services and general healthcare - Free contraception for minors: available through the healthcare system - Social safety net: reduces health disparities linked to poverty - Teacher autonomy: high-quality teachers with high salaries and academic status - Evidence-based policy: government decisions informed by THL data

docs.title: 3.3 Finland's Distinctive Strengths
docs.text:
1. The ONLY country in this 6-country panel where health education is:
  2. A mandatory, standalone subject at BOTH lower AND upper secondary level
  3. Can be examined at the national exit examination (ylioppilastutkinto)

  4. Requires teachers with subject-specific Master's degree qualifications

  5. World-class school health infrastructure: daily school nurse, school doctor protocol, school psychologist and social worker – all free and universal

  6. KiVa Koulu – one of the world's best-evidenced anti-bullying programs, embedded in schools and connected to health education

  7. Liikkuva koulu (Schools on the Move) – unique national program integrating movement throughout the school day; more evidence-based than typical PE-alone approaches

  8. National biennial health monitoring (THL Kouluterveyskysely, 260,000 students) – provides granular, school-level data to guide both policy and individual school action

  9. Assessment ethics: explicit legal protection from assessing personal values and health behaviors – unique in Europe

docs.title: 3.4 Challenges and What Finland Can Learn from Others
docs.text:
Finland's challenges: - Mental health crisis among girls: 31–34% moderate-to-severe anxiety (THL 2023) – despite excellent services - Rising e-cigarette use: curriculum and prevention programs need updating - Bullying still present: KiVa Koulu helps, but THL 2023 shows small increase - Physical activity inequality by gender: girls significantly less active than boys at all ages

What Finland could learn from other countries: - Ireland's Junior Cycle SPHE 2023: highly structured, modular approach to sexual health and LGBTQI+ topics – could update TE1 structure - France's EVARS 2025: specific, detailed programme for sexuality/relationships/pornography topics – more explicit structure than current Finnish practice - Portugal's UCC model: integration of health workers from community health centers into schools (Finland's school nurses are in-school, but inter-agency collaboration could be stronger)

docs.title: Finland – Terveystieto (Health Education): Curriculum Content in Lukio (NCC 2019)
1.1 Structure of Lukio
docs.text:
Lukio (general upper secondary school) in Finland is a voluntary 3-year programme (typically ages 16–19) that prepares students for the Ylioppilastutkinto (Finnish Matriculation Examination). The 2019 reform restructured the curriculum from courses to modules (opintojaksot), each worth 2 credits (ECTS-like units called op).

Key features: - Students must complete 150 credits (opintopistettä) total - Of these, ~118 credits are national compulsory or national elective - Health education (Terveystieto) contributes 6 credits as compulsory (3 modules × 2 credits) + optional additional modules - Health education can be taken as a ylioppilaskoe (matriculation exam subject) – voluntary but available

docs.title: 1.2 Terveystieto Structure in Lukio (NCC 2019)
docs.text: Module Finnish Name English Name Credits TE1 Terveys voimavarana Health as a Resource 2 op (mandatory) TE2 Terveys ja ympäristö Health and Environment 2 op (mandatory) TE3 Terveys ja yhteiskunta Health and Society 2 op (mandatory) Optional Koulun omat moduulit School-specific optional modules Variable

docs.title: 2. Module TE1: Terveys voimavarana (Health as a Resource)
2.1 Core Philosophy
docs.text: The salutogenic approach underpins this module: health is seen as a resource (voimavara) for life, not just the absence of disease. Students develop a holistic, multidimensional view of health: fyysinen, psyykkinen, sosiaalinen (physical, mental, social) – and increasingly environmental/ecological.

docs.title: 2.2 Learning Objectives
docs.text: Students will: - Understand health as a multidimensional, dynamic resource - Analyse individual, social and environmental factors affecting health - Develop ability to make evidence-based health decisions - Strengthen self-care skills and health literacy - Apply critical thinking to health information sources

docs.title: 2.3 Detailed Content
docs.text:
Health as a Concept: - World Health Organization (WHO) definition of health and its evolution - Salutogenesis (Antonovsky): sense of coherence (koherenssin tunne) as health resource - Dimensions of health: physical, mental, social, sexual, spiritual, environmental - Health inequalities: gender, socioeconomic, ethnic differences in health outcomes in Finland

Lifestyle and Health Promotion: - Physical activity in adulthood: WHO recommendations; sedentary behavior risks - Finnish nutrition recommendations for young adults (Valtion ravitsemusneuvottelukunta) - Sleep among students: Finnish university students and lukio students; sleep deprivation epidemic - Substance use in upper secondary: alcohol, tobacco, cannabis, vaping (updated THL Kouluterveyskysely 2023 data) - Screen time and digital well-being: social media, gaming, learning vs. entertainment

Mental Health as a Resource: - Positive mental health: flourishing, meaning, resilience - Stress in lukio: exam pressure, future anxiety, social stress - Burnout among students (koulu-uupumus): Finnish research; prevalence; prevention - Anxiety and depression: distinguishing normal sadness from clinical disorders - Mental health help in Finland: school nurse, school psychologist, YTHS (Finnish Student Health Service)

Sexual Health in Adulthood: - Sexual health as a lifelong resource: WHO definition - Healthy relationships: communication, mutual respect, equality, boundaries - Contraception choices for young adults: advantages/disadvantages of hormonal vs. barrier methods; IUDs; long-acting reversible contraception (LARC) - STI epidemiology in Finland: chlamydia trends (increasing); gonorrhea (increasing); HIV (stable) - STI testing services: accessible, free, and confidential for under-18s in Finland - Online sexual health resources: e-Loops; THL resources

docs.title: 3. Module TE2: Terveys ja ympäristö (Health and Environment)
3.1 Core Philosophy
docs.text: This module examines health from a community, social and environmental perspective. It addresses how the surrounding world – physical, social, digital, and ecological – affects health and well-being.

docs.title: 3.2 Learning Objectives
docs.text: Students will: - Understand the health-environment relationship from a systemic perspective - Analyse how social and cultural factors shape health behaviors - Critically evaluate the health implications of environmental factors - Connect individual health choices to community and planetary health (One Health)

docs.title: 3.3 Detailed Content
docs.text:
Physical Environment and Health: - Air quality (ilmanlaatu): indoor and outdoor pollution; effects on respiratory and cardiovascular health - Climate change and health: heat waves, extreme weather, vector-borne diseases (tick-borne diseases relevant in Finland), food security - One Health framework: interconnection of human health, animal health, and ecosystem health - Water quality; chemical exposure; environmental toxins

The School Environment: - School as a health-promoting environment (terveydenedistävä koulu) - Physical school environment: ergonomics, light, noise, indoor air quality - Social school environment: school climate (kouluyhteisö); sense of belonging; bullying prevention - THL 2023: 8–9% of basic education students and 1–4% of upper secondary students report weekly bullying - Violence prevention in school: Finnish anti-bullying programs (KiVa Koulu – internationally recognized)

Digital Environment and Health: - Social media and well-being: research on social comparison, FOMO, anxiety, body image - Cyberbullying: prevalence in Finland; legal consequences; support services - Digital health economy: mHealth apps; health data privacy; tracking and datafication of health - Algorithmic influence on health behavior and information intake - Gaming and online communities: positive potential (social connection, skills) vs. problematic use

Social and Cultural Environment: - How socioeconomic status affects health access and outcomes in Finland - Health-related inequalities by gender: girls' mental health crisis in Finnish THL data - Multiculturalism and health: immigrant health; access to services; cultural factors - Peer culture and social norms around health (drinking culture, diet ideals, fitness)

docs.title: 4. Module TE3: Terveys ja yhteiskunta (Health and Society)
4.1 Core Philosophy
docs.text: The third module connects health to the civic, political, economic, and ethical dimensions of society. Students develop health citizenship – the ability to understand and participate in health-related decision-making at community, national and global levels.

docs.title: 4.2 Learning Objectives
docs.text: Students will: - Understand the structure and principles of the Finnish healthcare system - Analyse health policies and ethical questions from multiple perspectives - Evaluate research evidence and media representations of health - Develop as active health citizens: advocacy, participation, rights

docs.title: 4.3 Detailed Content
docs.text:
Finnish Healthcare System: - Structure: primary care (terveyskeskukset), specialist care (sairaanhoitopiirit → hyvinvointialueet since 2023), private care - Welfare area reform (hyvinvointialueuudistus, 2023): restructuring of Finnish social and healthcare services into 21 welfare areas - Funding: tax-funded (sairausvakuutus, kela, municipal taxation) - Patient rights: informed consent; right to information; confidentiality; language rights - YTHS (Finnish Student Health Service): for lukio and university students; physical, mental, dental health

Health Policy and Prevention: - Finnish national health programs: Terveys 2015, Sosiaali- ja terveysministeriön strategia - Health promotion at population level: legislation (tobacco, alcohol, sugar tax discussions) - The Sote reform 2023: implications for access to services; regional health inequalities - Comparative health systems: Finland vs. other Nordic models vs. European models

Research, Evidence and Ethics: - How scientific research is conducted; reading health studies critically - Evidence-based medicine vs. pseudoscience: example case studies - Media and health: health journalism; how news shapes public health behavior - Big pharma and conflicts of interest: pharmaceutical marketing; over-medicalization - Bioethics: end-of-life care; euthanasia debate in Finland; organ donation - Ethics of genetic information: genetic testing; privacy; discrimination - AI in healthcare: ethical challenges; diagnostic AI; data concerns

Global Health Citizenship: - Global health: disease burden by world region; antimicrobial resistance globally - Finnish development aid and global health equity - UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs): health-related goals (SDG 3) - WHO and international health governance; pandemic preparedness (COVID-19 lessons)

docs.title: 5.1 Overview
docs.text:
Health education can be chosen as a ylioppilaskoeaine (matriculation exam subject). This is a distinctive feature of the Finnish system – few EU countries examine health education at the national exit exam level.

Exam structure: - Format: Written exam, essay-based + structured questions - Duration: 6 hours - Frequency: Twice a year (spring and autumn) - Examination board: Ylioppilastutkintolautakunta (YTL) - Language: Finnish or Swedish

Content of the exam: - Tests terveysosaaminen (health literacy) – not factual recall alone - Requires ability to analyse, evaluate, and synthesize health information - Current health issues and ethical dilemmas are part of the exam - Requires knowledge of TE1, TE2, TE3 content AND ability to apply it

Significance: - The existence of a national exam in health education signals the subject's academic seriousness in Finland - It motivates students to study health education deeply and systematically - This contrasts sharply with Ireland (no SPHE exam), Spain (no dedicated health exam), Portugal (Biologia yes, but not health ed per se), and Poland (no EZ exam)

docs.title: 6. Teacher Qualifications (Opettajan pätevyys)
docs.text:
Finnish health education teachers must meet specific qualifications – one of the strictest teacher qualification frameworks in the EU for this subject:

Requirement Detail Educational level Master's degree (maisterin tutkinto) Subject studies ≥60 ECTS in health education subject studies (aineopinnot) Pedagogical studies ≥60 ECTS in teacher education (pedagogiset opinnot) University providers University of Jyväskylä (primary); University of Tampere (secondary) Additional option Liikunta + terveystieto double qualification (common combination)

This is comparable to the requirement for physics or history teachers – health education is treated as a rigorous academic discipline in Finland, not as a life skills activity.

docs.title: Finland – Terveystieto: Methodology, School Health Services and Youth Health Statistics (2023–2025)
1. Pedagogical Philosophy of Finnish Health Education
1.1 Constructivist and Participatory Approach
docs.text:
Finnish health education pedagogy is rooted in constructivism (tiedon rakentaminen): students are not passive receivers of health information but active builders of health literacy. Key principles:

  • Student-centered (oppilaslähtöisyys): starting from students' own experiences, questions, and needs
  • Experiential (kokemusperäinen): learning from real-life health situations
  • Critical (kriittinen): questioning, evaluating, and analysing health information rather than accepting it uncritically
  • Values-based (arvopohjaissuus): developing personal responsibility, ethical reflection, respect for others
  • Participatory (osallistava): students contribute to designing learning environments and school well-being

docs.title: 1.2 Health as a Positive Resource (Salutogenesis)
docs.text:
Rather than focusing primarily on risks and diseases, Finnish health education uses a salutogenic orientation: - What makes people healthy and resilient? - What resources (voimavarat) do young people have? - How can strengths be built on?

This contrasts with purely pathogenic models that list diseases and dangers.

docs.title: 1.3 Assessment Ethics
docs.text:
One of the most distinctive features of Finnish health education assessment:

"Arviointi ei saa kohdistua oppilaan henkilökohtaisiin arvoihin, asenteisiin, temperamenttiin tai terveystottumuksiin." (Assessment shall not target the student's personal values, attitudes, temperament, or health behaviors.)

This means: - A student who smokes is not penalised in assessment for that behavior - A student who holds traditional views on sexuality is not penalised for those views - What is assessed is the ability to understand, analyse and critically evaluate health phenomena - This protects student privacy and avoids coercive or surveillance-based health education

docs.title: 2. Key Pedagogical Methods in Terveystieto
docs.text: Method Description Frequency Tutkiva oppiminen (Inquiry-based learning) Students formulate questions, research, and present health topics High Yhteistoiminnallinen oppiminen (Cooperative learning) Group investigation of health cases High Arvokeskustelu (Values discussion) Structured dialogue on ethical health dilemmas; no "right answer" imposed High Tapaustutkimus (Case study analysis) Analysis of fictional or anonymized health situations High Median analyysi (Media analysis) Critical examination of health advertising, social media content, news Medium Projektityö (Project work) Community health projects; school well-being surveys Medium Simulaatio (Simulation/role play) Communication in health situations; help-seeking scenarios Medium Reflektiivinen kirjoittaminen (Reflective writing) Personal health reflection journals (not assessed for content) Low-medium Asiantuntijavierailu (Expert visits) School nurse, doctor, psychologist, peer educator Variable Liikkuva opetus (Movement-integrated learning) Physical activity integrated into lessons Growing

docs.title: 3.1 Kouluterveydenhuolto (School Health Care System)
docs.text:
Finland has one of the best-developed school health care systems in Europe. It is free, universal, and integrated into the school environment:

Service What it provides Terveydenhoitaja (School nurse) Regular health checks; confidential consultations; sexual health advice; contraception; STI testing referrals; free condoms in many schools Lääkäri (Doctor) Obligatory health examinations (1st, 5th, 8th grade and lukio 1st year); specialist referrals Koulupsykologi (School psychologist) Mental health support; psychological assessments; crisis intervention Koulukuraattori (School social worker) Social support; family issues; preventing exclusion Erityisopettaja (Special education teacher) Learning difficulties; SEND support

Mandatory health examinations (terveystarkastukset): - Grades 1, 5, 8 (peruskoulu) + 1st year of lukio: comprehensive exam by school nurse + doctor - All other years: school nurse examination - All examinations include assessment of physical health, mental well-being, and social factors

docs.title: 3.2 YTHS (Opiskeluterveydenhuolto for Lukio)
docs.text: For lukio and higher education students: - YTHS (Ylioppilaiden terveydenhoitosäätiö – Finnish Student Health Service) provides healthcare for higher education students - For lukio students: school-based terveydenhuolto + additionally municipal health services

docs.title: 4. Key National Programs Related to Health Education
4.1 Liikkuva koulu (Schools on the Move)
docs.text:
• National program launched 2010, now universal across Finland
  • Aims to increase physical activity during the school day (breaks, active transport, movement-integrated lessons)
  • Connected to health education: demonstrates the value of physical activity experientially
  • Target: every student gets at least 60 minutes of physical activity during the school day
  • Evidence base: improves academic performance, concentration, and well-being

docs.title: 4.2 KiVa Koulu (KiVa Anti-Bullying Program)
docs.text:
• Internationally recognized Finnish anti-bullying program developed at University of Turku
  • Used in 90% of Finnish basic education schools
  • Involves all school staff + trained student groups (KiVa teams)
  • Contains elements of social skills, empathy, and health literacy relevant to Terveystieto
  • Connected to THL data: bullying prevention effectiveness measured by Kouluterveyskysely

docs.title: 4.3 Nuorisoasema (Youth Counseling Centers)
docs.text:
• Municipal services (youth counseling, mental health, substance abuse) for young people
  • Low-threshold: no referral needed; anonymous possible
  • Complementary to school health services

docs.title: 5. Youth Health Statistics: THL Kouluterveyskysely 2023
docs.text: The Kouluterveyskysely (School Health Promotion Study) is Finland's largest national health survey of young people, conducted by THL every 2 years. The 2023 wave reached approximately 260,000 students.

docs.title: 5.1 Mental Health (2023)
docs.text:
Indicator Grades 8–9 Upper Secondary / Vocational Notes Girls reporting moderate-to-severe anxiety 31–34% 31–34% Significantly higher than boys Boys reporting moderate-to-severe anxiety 7–8% 7–8% Gender gap is striking Students with good/excellent perceived health ~80% (most) ~80% Overall still majority positive Weekly bullying experiences (victims) 8–9% 1–4% Increased vs. 2021 Sleep < 8h on school nights (% declining) Improving Improving Positive trend vs. 2021

Key finding: The gender gap in anxiety is one of the most striking findings. Girls' mental health in Finland has deteriorated significantly over the last decade, much more so than boys'. This is a national health emergency addressed by multiple policies.

docs.text: Indicator Grades 8–9 Upper Secondary Meeting WHO daily 60 min recommendation ~20–25% (boys) Declining with age Girls meeting recommendation ~15% Further decline Significant increase in physical activity (2021→2023) ✅ Positive trend ✅ Most groups Screen time affecting sleep/eating 10–16% report this 10–16%

docs.title: 5.3 Substance Use (2023)
docs.text:
Substance Grades 8–9 Upper Secondary Alcohol (ever tried) Declining: ~30–40% ~60–70% Regular alcohol use Declining Declining E-cigarettes/vaping Increasing significantly Major upward trend Cannabis (ever tried) <10% ~15% Nicotine pouches (nikotiinipussit) New; emerging concern New

Key finding: While traditional alcohol and cigarette use has been declining, e-cigarette and nicotine pouch use is rising rapidly among Finnish teens – a major emerging issue for health education.

docs.title: 5.1 Terveysosaaminen (Health Literacy) – Ydinkonsepti
docs.text:
Suomalainen terveystieto rakentuu terveysosaamisen (health literacy) käsitteen ympärille:

"Terveysosaaminen on terveyteen liittyvien tietojen, taitojen, asenteiden ja toimintavalmiuksien kokonaisuus. Se sisältää kyvyn hankkia, ymmärtää, arvioida ja hyödyntää terveystietoa sekä tehdä terveydelle myönteisiä valintoja."

Terveysosaaminen = tiedot + taidot + asenteet + eettinen vastuu + kriittinen ajattelu

docs.title: 5.2 Arvioinnin Etiikka (Ethics of Assessment)
docs.text:
Suomalainen opetussuunnitelma määrittelee selkeästi:

"Arviointi ei saa kohdistua oppilaan henkilökohtaisiin arvoihin, asenteisiin, temperamenttiin tai terveystottumuksiin."

Tämä tarkoittaa, että oppilaan henkilökohtaisia terveysvalintoja ei arvioida – arvioidaan ainoastaan terveysosaaminen (kyky ymmärtää, analysoida ja kriittisesti arvioida terveyteen liittyviä ilmiöitä).

Tämä periaate erottaa Suomen mallin monista muista Euroopan maista.

docs.title: Finland – Terveystieto (Health Education): Curriculum Content in Peruskoulu (Grades 7–9), NCC 2014
1.1 Purpose and Philosophy
docs.text:
Terveystieto (Health Education) in grades 7–9 of Finnish basic education is built on the concept of terveysosaaminen (health literacy). This goes far beyond factual knowledge of health topics – it encompasses:

  • Tiedot (Knowledge): understanding health concepts, the body, disease, and the healthcare system
  • Taidot (Skills): practical capabilities to promote one's own and others' health
  • Asenteet (Attitudes): values, care for oneself and others, respect for diversity
  • Toimintavalmius (Readiness to act): critical decision-making; seeking help when needed

Key principle: Assessment does NOT evaluate the student's personal values, attitudes, temperament, or health behaviors. Only health literacy (terveysosaaminen) is assessed.

docs.title: 1.2 Position in the Curriculum
docs.text:
• Mandatory for ALL students in grades 7, 8, and 9
  • Stand-alone, independent subject (not integrated into biology or PE)
  • Total hours: determined by local curriculum (typically ~76 lessons over 3 years = approx. 2 lessons/week)
  • Taught by qualified health education teachers (Master's degree + 60 ECTS in health education subject studies + 60 ECTS in pedagogical studies)

docs.title: 2. Content Area S1: Kasvu ja kehitys (Growth and Development)
2.1 Overview
docs.text: This content area examines adolescent development from a holistic perspective – physical, emotional, psychological, and social. It recognizes the diversity and individual pace of development as natural.

docs.title: 2.2 Topics Covered
docs.text:
Identity and Self-Knowledge: - Construction of personal identity during adolescence: who am I, what do I value? - Self-image (minäkuva) and self-esteem (itsetunto): healthy vs. unrealistic self-image - Media and social media influence on body image and identity - Peer pressure and the need to belong vs. individual identity

Sexual Development and Sexuality (Seksuaalinen kehitys): - Puberty: physical and emotional changes in girls, boys, and those with diverse gender identities - The spectrum of sexual development: diversity and individual variation - Sexual identity: heterosexuality, homosexuality, bisexuality, asexuality, questioning - Gender identity: gender as a spectrum; transgender and non-binary identities; Finnish legal framework (Gender Recognition Act 2023) - Sexual rights: the right to one's own body; the right to say no; age of consent in Finland (16 years)

Emotional and Interaction Skills: - Recognizing and naming emotions (emotional literacy) - Empathy: understanding others' perspectives and needs - Communication in relationships: assertiveness, active listening - Managing conflict constructively: mediation, compromise - Loneliness and social exclusion: prevention and support

Stress and Crisis: - Age-appropriate stress: academic pressure, social expectations, future anxiety - Distinguishing normal stress from pathological stress - Resilience (resilienssi): coping strategies; bounce-back ability - Crises in adolescence: grief, family difficulties, trauma - Where to seek help: school nurse, school psychologist, crisis lines (Sekasin-chat, Mieli ry)

docs.title: 3. Content Area S2: Terveyteen vaikuttavat tekijät (Factors Affecting Health)
3.1 Overview
docs.text: This is the most extensive content area, covering both health-promoting and health-threatening factors. It has a strong preventive orientation while emphasizing positive health resources.

docs.title: 3.2 Lifestyle Factors (Elintavat)
docs.text:
Nutrition (Ravitsemus): - Finnish Nutrition Recommendations (Valtion ravitsemusneuvottelukunta): principles of a balanced diet - The Lautasmalli (plate model) and the nutrition wheel - Eating habits of Finnish adolescents: breakfast skipping (significant problem) - Critical analysis of food products and marketing - Eating disorders (syömishäiriöt): anorexia, bulimia, binge eating; risk factors; seeking help - Sustainable nutrition: environmental impact of food choices

Sleep and Rest (Uni ja lepo): - Adolescent sleep needs: 8–10 hours recommended - Consequences of sleep deprivation: academic performance, mental health, immune function - Sleep hygiene: routines, screen use before bed, light exposure - 2023 THL data: sleep improving but still significant issue for Finnish teens

Physical Activity (Liikunta): - WHO recommendations: ≥60 min/day of moderate-to-vigorous activity - Benefits of physical activity on mental health: depression, anxiety, self-esteem - Sedentary behavior: screen time; independent of physical activity as a separate risk factor - Finland's national programs: Liikkuva koulu (Schools on the Move) – movement-integrated school day - Sports club participation vs. independent activity

Mental Health (Mielenterveys): - Mental health as a resource: positive mental health (not just absence of disease) - Common mental health challenges in adolescence: anxiety, depression, loneliness - Warning signs and risk factors for mental health problems - THL 2023 data: 31–34% of 8th–9th grade girls report moderate-to-severe anxiety - Stigma and help-seeking: why young people don't ask for help; how to overcome barriers - Mental health services available: school nurse, school psychologist, youth counseling (nuorisoasema), crisis lines

docs.title: 3.3 Sexual Health (Seksuaaliterveys)
docs.text:
Contraception (Ehkäisy): - Methods of contraception: condom (primary + dual protection), hormonal methods (pill, ring, patch, implant, IUD), emergency contraception - Effectiveness of different methods; typical vs. perfect use - Access to contraception in Finland: school nurse (free condoms in many schools), health centers, sexual health clinics - Finnish law: under-18s can access contraception and STI testing without parental consent

STIs (Sukupuolitaudit / Seksitaudit): - Most common STIs in Finland: chlamydia (most common), gonorrhea, HPV, HIV/AIDS, herpes - Transmission routes; symptoms and asymptomatic infections - Testing and treatment: free STI testing available - HPV vaccination: part of Finland's national vaccination program (girls since 2013, all since 2020)

Sexual Violence and Harassment: - Definitions: sexual harassment, sexual assault, rape in Finnish law - Online sexual harassment: grooming, sextortion sharing intimate images without consent - Consent: what it means; how to communicate it; when it cannot be given - Resources: SERI (Sexual Violence Support Centre); Nollalinja (for intimate partner violence)

docs.title: 3.4 Substance Use and Addictions (Päihteet ja Riippuvuudet)
docs.text:
Alcohol: - Effects on the developing adolescent brain: neurological vulnerability under 25 - Finnish alcohol culture: context in Nordic society - Binge drinking (kertajuominen): prevalence; acute risks (alcohol poisoning, accidents, risky behavior) - Long-term health risks: liver disease, cancer, addiction - Finnish law: under-18 cannot buy or consume alcohol

Tobacco and Nicotine: - Cigarettes: composition; addiction (nicotine); health effects (lung cancer, COPD, cardiovascular disease) - E-cigarettes and vaping pods: rapidly increasing use among Finnish teens (THL 2023: significant rise) - Nicotine pouches (nikotiinipussit): new trend; regulation in Finland - Finnish tobacco legislation: smoke-free spaces; age restrictions

Cannabis: - Effects of cannabis on the adolescent brain: impaired memory, motivation, psychiatric risk - Legal status in Finland: illegal (unlike Portugal's decriminalization) - Trends: cannabis use in Finland lower than EU average (a matter of context for comparison)

Behavioral Addictions: - Gaming disorder (peliriippuvuus): WHO ICD-11 criteria; Finnish gaming culture - Social media addiction: FOMO, comparison loops, sleep disruption - Internet addiction: problematic internet use; THL 2023: 10–16% report sleep/eating affected by internet use - Gambling (rahapelaaminen): in Finland, Veikkaus monopoly + restriction system

docs.title: 3.5 Diseases and Accident Prevention (Sairaudet ja Tapaturmien Ehkäisy)
docs.text:
• Non-communicable diseases (NCD): type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, cancer – risk factors and prevention
  • Infectious diseases: vaccination policy (Finland has high vaccination coverage); seasonal flu; COVID-19 as case study
  • Antibiotic resistance: responsible use; Finnish context (Finland among lowest antibiotic users in EU)
  • Accident prevention: road safety; sports injuries; home accidents
  • First aid basics: CPR principles; calling 112; assisting in emergencies

docs.title: 4. Content Area S3: Terveys, yhteisöt ja yhteiskunta (Health, Communities and Society)
4.1 Overview
docs.text: This content area places health in its social, cultural, community, and global context. It fosters health-related citizenship.

docs.title: 4.2 Topics Covered
docs.text:
Environmental Health: - Physical environment: air quality; pollutants; climate change as a health issue (One Health connection) - Social environment: school climate (kouluyhteisö); bullying (THL 2023: 8–9% report weekly bullying) - Digital environment: online communities; digital well-being; cyberbullying

Media Literacy and Health Information: - Critical evaluation of health information: how to assess reliability of sources - Health misinformation and pseudoscience: identifying quackery; anti-vaccination claims - Social media and health: influencers promoting products; body image content - Evidence-based health information: THL, WHO, medical databases vs. commercial sources

Use of Healthcare Services (Terveyspalvelut): - Finnish healthcare system: school health services (kouluterveydenhuolto); health centers (terveyskeskus); hospitals; emergency (112) - Rights as a patient: free healthcare for minors; confidentiality - Student health services (opiskeluterveydenhuolto) - Mental health services: student counseling; crisis services; psychiatric services

Human Rights and Health: - Health as a fundamental right (Finnish Constitution; UN Declaration) - Health inequalities: socioeconomic factors; gender differences; ethnic minority health - Global health: international health organizations (WHO, UNICEF); global disease burden

docs.title: 5. Pedagogical Approach in Finnish Health Education
5.1 Core Pedagogical Methods
docs.text: Method Application in Terveystieto Inquiry-based learning Students research health questions and present findings Collaborative learning Group work on health scenarios; peer discussion Discussion and debate Structured discussion on ethical health dilemmas Case analysis Anonymous or fictional health situations Project-based learning Community health projects; school well-being projects Critical media analysis Analysis of health advertising, social media content Reflection and journaling Personal health reflection (not assessed for content)

docs.title: 5.2 Transversal Competencies (Laaja-alainen osaaminen)
docs.text: Terveystieto contributes to all 7 transversal competence areas of the Finnish NCC 2014: 1. Thinking and learning to learn (L1) 2. Cultural competence, interaction, self-expression (L2) 3. Taking care of oneself, managing daily life (L3) ← most directly linked 4. Multiliteracy (L4) ← media literacy in health 5. ICT competence (L5) 6. Working life competence and entrepreneurship (L6) 7. Participation, involvement, sustainable future (L7)

docs.text:
1. Opetushallitus (2014). Perusopetuksen opetussuunnitelman perusteet 2014 – Terveystieto (vuosiluokat 7–9). Helsinki: OPH. https://eperusteet.opintopolku.fi

docs.title: 🇫🇮 Suomi / Finland (FI) — Asiakirjarekisteri / Document Registry
docs.text:
Terveysopetuksen järjestelmä / Health Education System: Terveystieto — pakollinen oppiaine (Grades 7–9, Lukio) Bioregion: Nordic Reform Status: NCC 2014 (basic education) and NCC 2019 (upper secondary) in force; new Lukio NCC 2019 fully implemented

Tämä rekisteri sisältää kaikki Suomen osalta OneHealth EU -hankkeessa tunnistetut lähdeasiakirjat. This registry lists all source documents identified for Finland in the OneHealth EU project.

docs.title: System Overview
docs.text: Finland has one of Europe's most developed health education systems. Terveystieto (Health Education) is a mandatory standalone subject in the peruskoulu (basic school, grades 7–9, ages 13–16) and a mandatory/optional subject in the lukio (upper secondary, TE1 mandatory, TE2–TE3 optional). Finland introduced Terveystieto as a standalone subject already in 2001 — one of the earliest in Europe. The Finnish National Core Curriculum (NCC) defines the objectives and content for all subjects. The Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare (THL) provides the key health data. Finland is also notable for its school health nurse (kouluterveydenhoitaja) model with nurses present in all schools.

docs.title: 1. Perusopetuslaki 628/1998 — Basic Education Act
docs.text:
• Type: Act of Parliament / Laki | Year: 1998 (as amended)
  • Publisher: Opetus- ja kulttuuriministeriö (Ministry of Education and Culture)
  • Description: The foundational law governing Finnish basic education (perusopetus). Establishes Terveystieto as a mandatory subject in grades 7–9 (added by amendment in 2001). Defines the overall purposes of education including wellbeing, health, and equality.
  • Access (Finlex): https://www.finlex.fi/fi/laki/ajantasa/1998/19980628

docs.title: 2. Lukiolaki 714/2018 — Upper Secondary Education Act
docs.text:
• Type: Act of Parliament / Laki | Year: 2018
  • Publisher: Opetus- ja kulttuuriministeriö
  • Description: Governs upper secondary (lukio) education in Finland. Establishes the requirement for all students to complete TE1 (Terveystieto 1, 2 credits, mandatory) and optionally TE2–TE3. Sets the framework for the NCC 2019 curriculum for upper secondary.
  • Access (Finlex): https://www.finlex.fi/fi/laki/ajantasa/2018/20180714

docs.title: 3. Perusopetuksen opetussuunnitelman perusteet 2014 (NCC 2014) — Terveystieto vuosiluokat 7–9
docs.text:
• Täydellinen nimi / Full title: Perusopetuksen opetussuunnitelman perusteet 2014
  • Type: National Core Curriculum / Opetussuunnitelma | Year: 2014 (in force from 2016)
  • Publisher: Opetushallitus (Finnish National Agency for Education, EDUFI)
  • Description: The National Core Curriculum for basic education defines the objectives and core content of Terveystieto for grades 7–9. Content covers: health as a resource; physical, mental, social and environmental health; relationships and sexuality; substance prevention; health literacy; navigating the health system. Available in Finnish, Swedish, and English.
  • Access (EDUFI / OPS2016): https://www.oph.fi/fi/koulutus-ja-tutkinnot/perusopetuksen-opetussuunnitelman-perusteet
  • Direct PDF (Finnish): https://www.oph.fi/sites/default/files/documents/perusopetuksen_opetussuunnitelman_perusteet_2014.pdf

docs.title: 4. Lukion opetussuunnitelman perusteet 2019 (NCC 2019) — Terveystieto TE1, TE2, TE3
docs.text:
• Täydellinen nimi / Full title: Lukion opetussuunnitelman perusteet 2019
  • Type: National Core Curriculum | Year: 2019 (fully in force from 2021)
  • Publisher: Opetushallitus (EDUFI)
  • Description: The NCC for upper secondary education defines three Terveystieto courses: TE1 (mandatory, 2 credits): health and functional capacity, mental health, relationships and sexuality, health information literacy; TE2 (voluntary, 2 credits): health promotion, society, inequalities; TE3 (voluntary, 2 credits): deepened topics chosen by student. Assessment is grade-based at TE1.
  • Access (EDUFI): https://www.oph.fi/fi/koulutus-ja-tutkinnot/lukion-opetussuunnitelman-perusteet
  • Direct PDF (Finnish): https://www.oph.fi/sites/default/files/documents/lukion_opetussuunnitelman_perusteet_2019.pdf

docs.title: 5. Kouluterveyskysely — School Health Survey (THL, biennial)
docs.text:
• Type: National health survey / Kansallinen tutkimus | Year: Biennial (most recent 2023)
  • Publisher: Terveyden ja hyvinvoinnin laitos (THL — Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare)
  • Description: Finland's biennial Kouluterveyskysely (School Health Survey) — the most comprehensive source of data on Finnish children's health, wellbeing, sexual health, substance use, and school experiences. Results directly inform the development of Terveystieto and school health policy.
  • Access (THL): https://thl.fi/fi/tutkimus-ja-kehittaminen/tutkimukset-ja-hankkeet/kouluterveyskysely

docs.title: 6. HBSC Suomi 2022 — Health Behaviour in School-aged Children
docs.text:
• Type: Research report | Year: 2022 | Publisher: THL / WHO
  • Description: Finland's contribution to the international HBSC study. Coordinated by THL. Provides comparative international data alongside the domestic Kouluterveyskysely.
  • Access (THL): https://thl.fi/hbsc

docs.title: France – Éducation à la Santé : Cadre Légal et Contexte Réglementaire (2001–2025)
1.1 Données Générales
docs.text: Paramètre Valeur Pays France (FR) Population ~68 millions (2024) Langue officielle Français Type de système éducatif Fortement centralisé – Ministère de l'Éducation nationale (MEN) définit les programmes nationaux ; académies (en pratique ~26 rectorats) coordonnent la mise en œuvre Scolarité obligatoire 3–16 ans Collège (secondaire inférieur) 4 ans (6e–3e ; 11–15 ans) ← foco deste projeto Lycée général et technologique (GT) 3 ans (Seconde–Terminale ; 15–18 ans) ← foco Lycée professionnel 3 ans (CAP/Bac Pro) Examen final Baccalauréat (Bac) – réformé en 2019 (Bac 2021) Autorité curriculaire MEN / Conseil Supérieur des Programmes (CSP) Portail pédagogique Éduscol (eduscol.education.fr)

docs.title: 1.2 Spécificité : Système Centralisé, Mais École Autonome dans ses Actions
docs.text: Le modèle français combine : - Centralisation des programmes : les contenus d'enseignement sont définis nationalement (Bulletin Officiel) - Autonomie des établissements pour les actions éducatives en santé via le CESCE (Comité d'éducation à la santé, à la citoyenneté et à l'environnement) et le Parcours éducatif de santé (PES) - Absence de discipline autonome "Éducation à la santé" : les contenus sont répartis entre SVT, EPS, EMC et d'autres matières

docs.title: 2.1 Chronologie Législative
docs.text: Année Texte Objet 1998 Circulaire n° 98-234 du 19/11/1998 Premiers cadres de l'éducation à la santé en milieu scolaire 2001 Loi du 4 juillet 2001 (article L312-16 Code éducation) Obligation légale de 3 séances annuelles d'éducation à la sexualité à chaque niveau 2006 Circulaire n° 2006-197 du 30/11/2006 Organisation des actions éducatives en santé ; rôle du CESC 2016 Décret n° 2016-1855 Parcours éducatif de santé (PES) – généralisé à tous les niveaux 2021 Loi « Climat et Résilience » n° 2021-1104 (22/08/2021) CESC devient CESCE (ajout de l'environnement) 2022 Décret n° 2022-540 du 12 avril 2022 Précise les attributions du CESCE dans chaque établissement 2024 Nouveau programme EMC (BO juin 2024) Renouvellement des programmes d'Enseignement moral et civique 2025 Arrêté du 3 février 2025 (JO 5 fév. 2025) Programme national EVARS (Éducation à la vie affective, relationnelle et à la sexualité) – applicable dès la rentrée 2025

docs.title: 2.2 Textes Clés (Détails)
docs.text:
Loi du 4 juillet 2001 – Éducation à la sexualité (art. L312-16 Code de l'éducation) :

Donnée Valeur Obligation ≥ 3 séances annuelles par niveau (école, collège, lycée) Contenu Biologique, psycho-émotionnel, juridique/social Mise en œuvre Enseignants ou intervenants extérieurs qualifiés (associations agréées) Limite reconnue Rapport IGESR 2021 : faibles % d'élèves bénéficiant réellement des 3 séances Évolution 2025 Remplacé/complété par le programme EVARS (arrêté 3 fév. 2025)

Arrêté du 3 février 2025 – Programme national EVARS :

Donnée Valeur Nom complet Programme d'Éducation à la vie affective, relationnelle et à la sexualité (EVARS) Application Rentrée scolaire 2025-2026 Public cible Tous établissements scolaires (public + privé sous contrat) Format ≥ 3 séances annuelles structurées (progressif par niveau) Contenu Corps ; relations et émotions ; consentement ; IST/contraception ; numérique/médias URL Légifrance https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr (JO 5 février 2025)

docs.title: 3.1 Définition et Cadre
docs.text:
Le Parcours éducatif de santé (PES) est le cadre structurant de l'éducation à la santé en France depuis le Décret de 2016. Il concerne tous les élèves, de la maternelle au lycée, et se décline en 3 axes complémentaires :

Axe Description Éducation à la santé Compétences psychosociales ; choix éclairés ; comportements sains Prévention Actions spécifiques sur addictions, harcèlement, violences, santé mentale Protection de la santé Suivi médical à l'infirmerie ; visites médicales obligatoires ; aménagements pour élèves malades

docs.title: 3.2 Articulation avec les Programmes
docs.text: Le PES se nourrit des contenus de plusieurs disciplines : - SVT (Sciences de la Vie et de la Terre) → corps humain, reproduction, immunité - EPS (Éducation Physique et Sportive) → activité physique, bien-être, gestion de l'effort - EMC (Enseignement Moral et Civique) → valeurs, droits, citoyenneté, consentement - Physique-Chimie → nutrition au niveau moléculaire - EVARS (depuis 2025) → éducation à la vie affective et sexuelle (3 séances dédiées)

docs.title: 4. Le CESCE – Organe de Pilotage dans Chaque Établissement
4.1 Caractérisation
docs.text:
Le Comité d'éducation à la santé, à la citoyenneté et à l'environnement (CESCE) est une instance obligatoire dans chaque lycée (et dans les collèges). Il remplace depuis 2022 l'ancien CESC.

Composition : - Chef d'établissement (président) - Personnels d'enseignement, d'éducation, de santé et sociaux - Représentants des élèves - Représentants des parents d'élèves - Partenaires extérieurs (associations, professionnels de santé)

Missions : - Définir le programme d'actions EpS adapté aux besoins spécifiques de l'établissement - S'inscrire dans le Projet d'établissement - Articuler le PES avec les dispositifs nationaux (programme pHARe anti-harcèlement, EVARS, etc.) - Prévention des conduites addictives, promotion de la santé mentale, lutte contre les violences

docs.title: 5. Structure du Système Scolaire Français (niveaux pertinents pour l'EpS)
5.1 Collège (11–15 ans)
docs.text:
Niveau Équivalent Âge 6e 1ère année de collège 11–12 ans 5e 2e année de collège 12–13 ans 4e 3e année de collège 13–14 ans 3e 4e année de collège (Brevet) 14–15 ans

Examen : Brevet des collèges (DNB) – fin de 3e

docs.title: 5.2 Lycée (15–18 ans)
docs.text:
Niveau Équivalent Âge Seconde 1ère année du lycée 15–16 ans Première 2e année du lycée 16–17 ans Terminale 3e année du lycée 17–18 ans

Examen : Baccalauréat (Bac 2021, réforme Blanquer) – partiellement en cours d'année (épreuves de spécialité en 1re) + épreuves terminales

docs.title: 6. Institutions Clés en Éducation pour la Santé
docs.text: Institution Rôle MEN (Ministère de l'Éducation nationale) Programmes nationaux ; circulaires ; Éduscol ; formation des enseignants Santé publique France Données épidémiologiques ; campagnes de prévention ; ressources pédagogiques INSERM Recherche en santé ; données scientifiques OFDT (Observatoire français des drogues et des tendances addictives) Données sur les addictions chez les jeunes ; EnCLASS HAS (Haute Autorité de Santé) Recommandations médicales et de prévention EHESP Recherche en santé publique ; coordinateur de l'enquête EnCLASS Réseau Canopé Ressources pédagogiques nationales Académies (rectorats) Déclinaison locale des politiques nationales CESCE (dans chaque établissement) Pilotage local de l'EpS Infirmier·ère scolaire Présence médico-sociale dans l'établissement Assistants sociaux scolaires Soutien social aux élèves et familles

docs.title: 7. Hiérarchie Normative (EpS en France)
docs.text:
Code de l'éducation (loi L312-16 et autres articles)
        ↓
Décrets et arrêtés ministériels (dont décret PES 2016 ; arrêté EVARS 2025)
        ↓
Programmes nationaux des disciplines (SVT, EPS, EMC → BO – Bulletin Officiel)
        ↓
Circulaires et instructions pédagogiques (Éduscol)
        ↓
Projet d'établissement + Programme CESCE (niveau de chaque école/lycée)
        ↓
Programmation didactique des enseignants (cours, séances EVARS, projets interdisciplinaires)

docs.title: France – Éducation à la Santé : Contenus Curriculaires par Discipline (Collège + Lycée)
1. Vue d'Ensemble : Comment l'EpS est Distribuée dans les Disciplines
docs.text:
La France n'a pas de discipline unique "Éducation à la santé". Les contenus de santé sont répartis entre plusieurs disciplines, selon le schéma suivant :

Discipline Niveaux Charge EpS Contenus de santé principaux SVT (Sciences de la Vie et de la Terre) Collège + Lycée (tronc commun + spécialité) Forte Corps humain, santé, reproduction, immunité, génétique médicale EPS (Éducation Physique et Sportive) Collège + Lycée Forte Activité physique, bien-être, corps, gestion de l'effort, santé mentale EMC (Enseignement Moral et Civique) Collège + Lycée Modérée Libertés, droits du corps, consentement, violences, discriminations EVARS Collège + Lycée (depuis 2025) 3 séances/an Vie affective, sexualité, consentement, IST, numérique/pornographie Physique-Chimie Collège + Lycée Légère Nutrition moléculaire ; chimie du corps EPI / Projets interdisciplinaires Collège Variable Projets santé transversaux (nutrition, bien-être, addictions)

docs.title: 2. SVT (Sciences de la Vie et de la Terre) – Principal Porteur de Contenus de Santé
2.1 Au Collège (6e–3e)
docs.text:
6e : - Organisation du vivant : cellules, organes, tissus ; unité et diversité du vivant - Alimentation et digestion : rôle des nutriments ; système digestif

5e : - Corps humain et alimentation : besoins nutritifs ; métabolisme de base - Respiration : oxyhémoglobine ; échanges gazeux ; impact du tabac sur les poumons - Relations entre organismes : microorganismes bénéfiques vs. pathogènes

4e : - Reproduction humaine : appareil reproducteur ; puberté (physiologie et psychologie des changements) ; cycles de reproduction - Sexualité et santé : méthodes contraceptives (mécanismes, efficacité, accessibilité) ; infections sexuellement transmissibles (IST) : VIH, hépatites ; prevention des IST - Système nerveux : transmission de l'influx nerveux ; réflexes ; effets des stupéfiants sur le cerveau

3e : - Génétique et ADN : transmission des caractères héréditaires ; mutations ; maladies génétiques - Immunité : système immunitaire inné et acquis ; vaccination (mécanismes, polémiques) ; transplantation - Résistances aux antibiotiques : mécanismes ; conséquences en santé publique - Biotechnologies médicales : insuline, vaccins OGM ; thérapie génique (perspectives)

docs.title: 2.2 Au Lycée – Tronc Commun : Seconde
docs.text:
• Corps humain et santé : procréation, contraception, contrôle hormonal
  • Microorganismes et immunité : réponse immunitaire ; vaccins ; limites de la médecine
  • Génétique : variation génétique comme base de l'évolution + maladies génétiques
  • Alimentation et santé : nutrition cellulaire ; métabolisme basal vs. besoins sportifs

docs.title: 2.3 Au Lycée – Spécialité SVT : Première
docs.text:
• Variation génétique et santé : mutations somatiques ; cancérisation ; oncogènes et gènes suppresseurs de tumeur ; traitements (immunothérapie, chimiothérapie)
  • Système immunitaire (approfondissement) : inflammation ; réaction immunitaire adaptative ; antigènes ; anticorps ; vaccins et sérums ; maladies auto-immunes
  • Résistances aux antibiotiques : mécanismes moléculaires ; implications en santé publique globale (One Health)
  • Génétique de la conservation : diversité génétique ; effets de la consanguinité

docs.title: 2.4 Au Lycée – Spécialité SVT : Terminale
docs.text:
• Comportement, mouvement et cerveau : neurobiologie du mouvement ; système nerveux central ; cerveau fragile (traumatismes, substances psychoactives)
  • Réponse au stress : axe hypothalamo-hypophysaire-surrénalien ; cortisol ; stress chronique et santé
  • Biologie moléculaire avancée : expression du génome ; modulation épigénétique
  • Biodiversité et santé globale : connexions One Health (santé humaine – écosystèmes)

docs.title: 3. EPS (Éducation Physique et Sportive) – Corps, Bien-Être et Santé Active
3.1 Rôle de l'EPS dans l'EpS
docs.text:
L'EPS en France ne se limite pas à la pratique sportive. Elle vise explicitement la construction d'un rapport positif au corps, à la santé et à l'effort tout au long de la vie. La santé est un enjeu structurant de la compétence "Agir, s'exprimer, comprendre dans une activité physique" du Collège.

Note importante : En France, la note d'EPS compte dans la moyenne du Baccalauréat (via le contrôle continu). Cela assure une plus grande valorisation de la discipline vs. l'Espagne où elle ne compte pas.

docs.title: 3.2 Contenus de Santé au Collège (EPS)
docs.text:
• Connaissance de soi et de son corps : sensations corporelles ; limites personnelles ; récupération
  • Sécurité physique : échauffement, prévention des blessures, règles de sécurité
  • L'effort et la fatigue : adaptation aux efforts d'intensité variable
  • Hygiène corporelle et soin du corps après l'activité physique
  • Les bienfaits de l'activité physique : cardiovasculaires, psychologiques, sociaux

docs.title: 3.3 Contenus de Santé au Lycée (EPS)
docs.text:
Axe "Entretien de soi" (compétence prioritaire) : - Conception et réalisation d'un programme d'entraînement personnel - Physiologie de l'effort : VO₂max, fréquence cardiaque, seuils aérobie/anaérobie - Alimentation et nutrition sportive : macronutriments, timing des repas, hydratation - Récupération active, sommeil et performance - Posture et ergonomie : prévention des troubles musculo-squelettiques (TMS) - Activité physique et santé mentale : endorphines, anxiété, dépression, estime de soi

Axe "Agir en citoyen" : - Dopage : substances interdites ; effets sur la santé ; enjeux éthiques - Corps et médias : image corporelle ideale vs. santé réelle ; injonctions esthétiques - Sport inclusif : accessibilité, handisport, mixité

docs.title: 3.4 Secourisme (PSC1) – Prévention et Secours Civiques
docs.text: En France, la formation PSC1 (Prévention et Secours Civiques niveau 1) est intégrée dans le cursus scolaire pour de nombreux élèves : - Reconnaître une situation d'urgence ; alerter les secours (15, 18, 112) - Réanimation Cardio-Pulmonaire (RCP) + utilisation du Défibrillateur Automatisé Externe (DAE) - Position Latérale de Sécurité (PLS) - Compression locale et hémorragies

docs.title: 4. EMC (Enseignement Moral et Civique) – Dimension Éthique et Citoyenne de la Santé
4.1 Structure au Lycée (Réforme 2019 + Nouveau programme 2024)
docs.text: À partir de la rentrée 2024–2025, un nouveau programme d'EMC est progressivement mis en place. Les thèmes couverts restent structurés par classe : - Seconde : La liberté (inclut : libertés corporelles ; normes sociales ; pressions) - Première : La société (inclut : violences ; discriminations ; lien social ; inégalités de santé) - Terminale : La démocratie (inclut : accès aux soins ; santé publique et choix politiques ; bioéthique)

docs.title: 4.2 Contenus de Santé en EMC
docs.text:
• Droits du corps : intégrité physique comme droit fondamental ; respect de l'autre
  • Consentement : dans les relations affectives et sexuelles ; dans les soins médicaux
  • Violence et discrimination : violences sexuelles et sexistes (VSS) ; harcèlement ; cyberharcèlement
  • Égalité de genre : stéréotypes ; inégalités de santé selon le genre
  • Bioéthique : don d'organes ; interruption médicale de grossesse ; fin de vie (loi Claeys-Leonetti) ; bioéthique des biotechnologies
  • Inégalités sociales de santé : impact de la précarité ; déserts médicaux
  • Libertés et contraintes : port du masque (COVID) ; vaccinations ; refus de traitement

docs.title: 5. EVARS – Programme National 2025 (Éducation à la Vie Affective, Relationnelle et à la Sexualité)
5.1 Cadre et Nouveauté
docs.text: L'EVARS est le nouveau programme national fixé par l'arrêté du 3 février 2025, applicable à la rentrée 2025-2026. Il remplace et structure l'obligation des "3 séances" de la loi de 2001, en proposant un cadre progressif et cohérent de la maternelle à la terminale.

docs.title: 5.2 Contenus au Collège (11–15 ans)
docs.text:
6e–5e (début collège) : - Le corps en développement : puberté (changements physiques, émotionnels) ; respect du corps d'autrui - Émotions et relations : identifier et exprimer ses émotions ; amitiés, atractions, premières relations - Consentement : apprendre à dire oui/non ; respecter le refus des autres ; signaler les situations problématiques

4e–3e (fin collège) : - Sexualité et santé reproductive : anatomie ; cycles menstruels ; méthodes contraceptives ; prévention des IST - Diversité : orientations sexuelles ; identités de genre ; non-discrimination - Violences sexuelles et sexistes : définition ; cycle de la violence ; comment réagir ; ressources - Numérique : sexting (qu'est-ce que c'est, risques) ; pornographie (réalité vs. fiction) ; cyberviolences ; consentement dans l'espace numérique

docs.title: 5.3 Contenus au Lycée (15–18 ans)
docs.text:
Seconde : - Santé sexuelle et reproductive avancée : IST (épidémiologie, prévention, test) ; PrEP ; contraception d'urgence - Consentement et droit : législation française ; définition juridique du viol (sans consentement) - Corps et image : pressions sociales, médias, pornographie ; dysmorphies corporelles

Première–Terminale : - Relations saines à l'âge adulte : communication dans le couple ; jalousie pathologique ; co-dépendance - Violences dans les relations intimes : violences conjugales ; cycle de l'emprise ; ressources (3919, FNSF) - Droit à la santé sexuelle : IVG en France (droit constitutionnel depuis 2024) ; droits LGBTQIA+ - Parentalité et projet de vie : stérilité ; PMA (procréation médicalement assistée) ; adoption - Pornographie et représentations : impact sur les stéréotypes de genre et d'orientation sexuelle

docs.title: 6.1 Physique-Chimie
docs.text:
• Chimie de l'alimentation : molécules nutritives, additifs, conservateurs
  • Toxicologie de base : effets de l'alcool, du tabac sur l'organisme (niveau moléculaire)
  • Médicaments : principes actifs, pharmacocinétique basique

docs.title: 6.2 Philosophie (Terminale)
docs.text: La Philosophie est obligatoire pour tous les élèves de Terminale en France (≠ Espagne où c'est optionnel au lycée). Elle aborde : - Bioéthique : autonomie, consentement, fin de vie - Liberté et déterminisme : responsabilité personnelle en matière de santé - Justice et inégalités : accès aux soins ; discrimination médicale - Le corps : corps-objet vs. corps-sujet (Merleau-Ponty) ; phénoménologie de la maladie

docs.title: 6.3 Sciences Économiques et Sociales (SES) – Spécialité Lycée
docs.text:
• Inégalités sociales de santé : déterminants socioéconomiques de la santé
  • Systèmes de santé comparés (Europe) : NHS, Assurance maladie, système bismarckien vs. beveridgien
  • Coût de la maladie pour la société ; enjeux du vieillissement de la population

docs.title: 6.4 EPI (Enseignements Pratiques Interdisciplinaires) – Collège
docs.text: Au collège, les EPI permettent des projets transversaux sur des thèmes de santé : - Projet "Alimentation et développement durable" (SVT + Géo) - Projet "Corps, sport et santé" (EPS + SVT) - Projet "Réseaux sociaux et bien-être mental" (EMC + Informatique/SNT)
